prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The manifesto outlines a programme to modernise public services, strengthen the economy, raise living standards, and reform governance.

Education
- Make education the top priority: reduce class sizes for 5–7-year-olds to 30 or fewer (funded by ending assisted places), guarantee nursery places for all four-year-olds, and focus on literacy and numeracy with clear targets and baseline assessments.
- Modernise comprehensives through setting by ability; intervene in failing schools with “fresh start” measures; create Education Action Zones; integrate special educational needs where appropriate.
- Connect schools to the internet (National Grid for Learning), upskill teachers in IT, and expand lifelong learning via a University for Industry and Individual Learning Accounts.
- Improve teacher training, induction, leadership standards, and establish a General Teaching Council.
- Reform higher education finance with fair, income-related repayments.
- Increase the share of national income spent on education over a Parliament as welfare costs fall.

Economy, tax, and welfare to work
- Deliver macroeconomic stability with a low-inflation target; reform monetary policy decision-making; follow a fiscal “golden rule” and keep debt prudent.
- Keep basic and top income tax rates unchanged for five years; aim for a 10p starting rate long term; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%; promote saving and investment (new ISAs; review of corporate and capital gains tax).
- Work within existing spending limits for two years; conduct spending reviews to shift resources from failure to investment.
- Fund a welfare-to-work programme via a windfall levy, moving 250,000 under-25s from benefits into jobs, education, training, or an environmental taskforce; incentivise hiring of the long-term unemployed; provide tailored help for lone parents; tackle benefit fraud.

Business, work, and pay
- Toughen competition law; improve the Private Finance Initiative; support small firms (cut late payment, reduce red tape, strengthen Business Links); create Regional Development Agencies; back science, design, and green technologies.
- Introduce a sensibly set national minimum wage advised by a Low Pay Commission; enable union recognition where a majority votes for it.

Health
- End the internal market; cut bureaucracy and reinvest in patient care; reduce waiting lists by 100,000 as a first step; eliminate waits for cancer surgery; increase NHS spending in real terms annually.
- Strengthen primary care commissioning, use multi-year agreements, and measure quality outcomes.
- Ban tobacco advertising; create an independent Food Standards Agency; promote public health and telemedicine.

Crime and justice
- Halve the time from arrest to sentence for persistent young offenders; replace repeat cautions with a single final warning; create Youth Offender Teams; introduce parental responsibility orders.
- Decentralise the prosecution service; set sentencing guidelines and improve consistency; focus police time on frontline work; support victims; coordinate anti-drugs action with testing and treatment orders.
- Provide a free parliamentary vote on banning handguns.

Families, housing, and pensions
- Develop a national childcare strategy; support reasonable working time, holiday, and unpaid parental leave; retain universal Child Benefit (uprated with prices).
- Protect homeowners (address gazumping costs); reinvest council house sale receipts in new and refurbished homes; license HMOs; introduce commonhold; restore a duty to help the unintentionally homeless.
- Protect the basic state pension (uprated with prices); promote stakeholder and occupational pensions; retain SERPS as an option; establish a Royal Commission on long-term care; strengthen carers’ support and care inspection.

Environment, transport, culture
- Make every department a “green” department; set an integrated transport policy; strengthen rail regulation and create a rail authority; develop a public/private partnership for the Underground; improve buses, safety for walking and cycling, and cut vehicle emissions; review the roads programme.
- Support rural services (including the Post Office), access to the countryside, wildlife protection, and animal welfare (free vote on hunting).
- Create NESTA to back young talent; protect school playing fields; reform lottery distribution and seek a not-for-profit operator at relet; balance media regulation while sustaining public service broadcasting.

Constitution and rights
- End hereditary voting rights in the second chamber; modernise the Commons; reform party funding transparency; hold a referendum on the voting system; introduce Freedom of Information.
- Devolve power to Scotland and Wales following referendums; create a London mayor and strategic authority; develop English regional chambers and possible elected assemblies by consent; strengthen local government with “best value” and performance plans.
- Incorporate the European Convention on Human Rights into UK law; advance enforceable civil rights for disabled people; reform Legal Aid; streamline immigration and asylum procedures.

Northern Ireland
- Support the peace process, human rights, fair policing, and economic development; combat terrorism.

Europe, defence, and foreign policy
- Lead EU reform (complete the single market, enlarge to new members, reform CAP/CFP, increase transparency); retain the veto on key areas while considering QMV where beneficial; sign the Social Chapter.
- Approach the single currency by economic test, with Cabinet, Parliament, and a referendum required.
- Base defence on NATO; conduct a strategic defence and security review; retain the nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral arms control; ban anti-personnel landmines; tighten arms export controls; support defence diversification.
- Reform the UN; prioritise development with a new department, shift aid to the poorest, reaffirm the 0.7% target, support debt relief; re-engage with UNESCO; centre foreign policy on human rights and an international criminal court; target a 20% CO2 cut by 2010 and lead on climate negotiations.

Five headline pledges
- Cut class sizes for 5–7-year-olds to 30 or fewer.
- Halve the time from arrest to sentencing for persistent young offenders.
- Cut NHS waiting lists by treating 100,000 extra patients, funded by savings from red tape.
- Get 250,000 under-25s off benefit and into work, funded by a windfall levy.
- No rise in income tax rates; cut VAT on heating to 5%; keep inflation and interest rates as low as possible.
